title: The Wide Frame
summary: The film stops being wallpaper and becomes the subject: one hard-edged widescreen band (2.76:1, the widest cinema format) that the page's own hairline opens, with the statement set inside it like a film's title card and the action on flat graphite below.
video: NOW (mockup): there is no new footage yet, so the band uses the existing film plate (img/film-room.webp) inside a .km-film confined to the band (1440 × 522). It is framed as an over-the-shoulder shot: the man seen from behind is the subject, his head, ear and collar dark against a lit wall just right of centre, the colleague he faces soft beyond his shoulder, a window at the right edge. His dark head sits behind the light word 'problem.' on purpose, so the accent always has shadow behind it. It is graded like footage rather than frosted flat: blur 8px (it starts at 12px and pulls focus once as the band opens), a light frost (.08), deeper blacks, warm practical light, a soft lens vignette and fine moving grain. Two things move: a slow sideways dolly (64px each way over 36 seconds, then back, so the loop is seamless), and a passer-by close to the lens, a soft dark shoulder that crosses the frame in about nine seconds once every thirty. Everything is CSS transforms, with no canvas: with the hero on screen the page's main thread spends under 1ms a second on it. It pauses when the hero is scrolled off screen and shows a still frame for visitors who ask for reduced motion. FOR LAUNCH: commissioned anamorphic 4K footage, shot at 2.39:1 and cropped to 2.76:1. One continuous 36–40 second slow sideways dolly along a glass-walled working session at night, shot through frosted glass so the softness is real optics, with someone passing close to the lens once. Graded graphite with warm practical lights, cut as a seamless (or ping-pong) loop, muted, playsinline, with the poster on the over-the-shoulder frame. The <video> replaces .km-film__plate inside the same band; nothing else changes.

reference.borrowed: Titan: a two-tone headline with dark footage of people held in a hard crop, which is what makes it read as cinema rather than wallpaper. Oryzo (refs/hero-r6-4.webp): footage cut by a hard flat seam, so the film has edges and flat colour does the structural work. Harvey (refs/hero-r6-10.webp) is the category default to move away from: full-bleed dark film of people at work under a left headline.
reference.kelwin: The band is full width and exactly 2.76:1, and its edges are Kelwin hairlines with four registration marks at the margins. The headline sits inside the band as a title card rather than above it, so the band frames the whole hero (not a film strip beneath a headline). The action sits on flat graphite with no wash. The opening is built from the page's hairline grammar, not from a video-player effect.

motion: entrance (about 2.5s): the nav hairline draws left to right (0.1–0.8s) and its two registration marks appear. At 0.7s it splits: a second hairline peels away and slides 523px down to the band's lower edge (1.1s). The film and the title card are revealed behind it, so a line opens into a picture, and the lens pulls focus once (12px to 8px). The label and the two lines of the statement rise inside the opening and the red rule draws; the lower marks appear as the line lands; then the lede, the doors and the audit note settle on the flat bar (1.8–2.5s).

ambient: only the film moves: a slow sideways dolly (64px each way over 36 seconds, about 3.5px a second), one passer-by close to the lens every 30 seconds (a nine-second pass, then the shot holds), and the grain. Nothing outside the band moves.

on the live site: the band holds a muted, looping background video. It pauses when the hero is off screen and resumes when it comes back. The band never pins; the page continues with reveal-on-scroll only.
reduced motion: the band is open on a still frame, with no entrance, no dolly, no passer-by and no grain.
addressed: The video is now the hero, not the wallpaper behind it. It plays in a hard-edged widescreen frame, like the opening title of a brand film. Serious enterprise and defence firms present themselves this way; agencies fill the whole screen with footage.
It reads as real footage rather than a dim photo: a working session seen over one man's shoulder, a slow camera move, someone passing close to the lens, and the lens finding focus as the frame opens.

It looks proprietary to Kelwin: the frame is drawn with the same hairlines and registration marks as every diagram further down the page, and it opens from the nav line itself. There are no player controls, captions or timecodes.

It is easier to read and to act on. The lede, the two buttons and the audit note sit on flat graphite under the film, crisp, instead of floating over the darkest part of the picture. The words and the reading path are the ones you approved, and the red button sits above the fold on 1440 × 900 and 1280 × 800 screens.
notes: Stage 960 = 96 nav + 522 band (y 96–618, full bleed, 1440/522 = 2.76:1) + 342 flat bar. Hairlines run margin to margin along the film's top and bottom edges (y 95 and 618, --line-2), with + marks at (64, 95), (1376, 95), (64, 618) and (1376, 618). Inside the band: the label at y 180, the 116px two-line statement at y 232–455, and the 48×2 red rule at y 495. On the bar: the 20px lede in cols 8–12 at y 666–756, the doors at y 784–840 (primary bottom 840 of 900 at 1440×900; 747 of 800 at 1280×800), and the audit note in cols 1–4, bottom-aligned with the doors as in every section head. Red: the two label squares, the rule and the primary only. Gradients exist only inside .km-film (the left scrim, its bottom-strip mask and the lens vignette). Contrast, measured at the brightest pixel under each line across ±72px of dolly (wider than the live ±64px), in both skins: 'Revenue is an' ≥ 9.4:1, 'architectural' ≥ 4.1:1, the light 'problem.' ≥ 3.1:1 (≥ 4.2:1 for 95% of its pixels; large text needs 3:1), the label ≥ 7.7:1. The lede, doors and note sit on flat graphite. Review pass, round 6: (1) a defect fixed: the plate ended before the frame did, so at one end of the dolly a grey strip of bare backing showed at the band's right edge (about 50px in the first build). The plate now repeats sideways; the stand-in is mirror-symmetric, so the window simply continues. (2) Reframed at ×1.15 so the man seen from behind reads as a person (head, ear, collar) right of centre, instead of a dark blob cropped by the top edge. (3) Graded like footage: frost .16 → .08, contrast 1.16 → 1.32, brightness 1.34, saturation .92, plus a soft lens vignette inside the film. (4) The dolly is now 64px each way over 36s (about 3.5px a second); 48px over 40s was too slow to register. (5) The walker, a small dark figure lost against the dark scene, is now a passer-by close to the lens: larger, softer, head out of frame, one nine-second pass every 30 seconds. Performance: with the hero on screen the main thread spends 0.7ms a second on it (compositor-only transforms); off screen the dolly, passer-by and grain are paused. The mirrored half of the stand-in plate stays under the scrim at the far left; real footage removes the need for it. On the live site the closed band should be the initial render when motion is allowed, so the opening never flashes the final state first.
story: The claim, said once, in a frame: “Revenue is an architectural problem.” After this the page stops asserting and starts showing.
